papers.title: Generalized supremum convolutions on the tensor product of unit intervals: t-conorms and triangle functions
papers.abstract: The complete-lattice tensor product $\mathbb{E}=[0,1]\otimes[0,1]$ arises naturally in the algebra of truth values for type-2 fuzzy sets. For a monotone surjective map $S$ that is continuous on $[0,1[^2$ and a monotone map $T$ having $1$ as identity, we consider the generalized supremum convolution \[ (f\otimes_{_{S,T}}g)(x)=\sup_{S(u,v)=x}T(f(u),g(v)) \] on $\mathbb{E}$. Rather than assuming classical algebraic structures for $S$ and $T$ from the outset, we ask when they are forced by requiring the induced convolution itself to be a t-conorm. We prove that $\otimes_{_{S,T}}$ is a t-conorm on $\mathbb{E}$ if and only if $S$ is a continuous t-conorm and either $S=\max$ or $T$ is a right-continuous t-norm; in the exceptional case $S=\max$, the convolution is simply the pointwise maximum for every admissible $T$. The same convolution mechanism also yields an order-dual description of triangle functions on the space of distance distribution functions $\Delta^+$. Using an order-reversing isomorphism between $\Delta^+$ and a boundary variant of $\mathbb{E}$, we show that $\tau_{_{T^*,L}}$ is a triangle function precisely when $L$ is a continuous t-conorm with no zero divisor and, unless $L=\max$, $T^*$ is a left-continuous t-conorm; moreover, when $L\neq\max$, continuity of $\tau_{_{T^*,L}}$ is equivalent to continuity of $T^*$. This resolves the remaining $\tau_{_{T^*,L}}$ part of the Schweizer--Sklar problem.

papers.title: Beyond left-continuity: t-norms on the fuzzy unit interval induced by pairs of t-norms
papers.abstract: We define a binary operation $T_1\star T_2$ on the fuzzy unit interval $\I$ by extending the natural action of $T_1$ and $T_2$ on step functions. When both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are left-continuous, this operation coincides with the tensor product of the corresponding quantales and therefore yields a t-norm on $\I$. Without left-continuity, the situation becomes more subtle. We prove that if at least one of the two t-norms is continuous, then $T_1\star T_2$ is still a t-norm on $\I$. We also show by counterexample that continuity cannot simply be dropped. The operation $\DN$ fails to be associative. On the other hand, $T_D\star T_D$ is a t-norm despite $T_D$ being neither continuous nor left-continuous, indicating that continuity is not a necessary condition.

papers.title: The maximal determinant of order 15 over the third roots of unity
papers.abstract: We prove that the largest absolute determinant of a $15\times15$ matrix with entries in $\{1,\omega,\omega^2\}$, where $\omega^3=1$ and $\omega\ne1$, is $120932352\sqrt{19}$. A matrix attaining this value was already known; the issue is maximality. The proof follows the Gram-matrix search method used in the real maximal-determinant problem. A sharp determinant bound in terms of the off-diagonal Gram energy, combined with Eisenstein congruences and a published classification of difference matrices, reduces a strict improvement to 23 possible energies. Componentwise Schur bounds and exact support catalogues then leave a small number of cases, excluded by orthogonality, rank, and spectral-intertwining conditions. We present the finite tests in a common framework and supply their replay programs. For the displayed extremizer we give a dephased representative, its Gram matrix and spectrum, and an exact computation of its monomial automorphism group, which has order 1008. The proof determines the value of the maximum, but does not classify all equality cases.

papers.title: Integration by differentiation
papers.abstract: In this note, we address a traditional pedagogical asymmetry between algorithmic differentiation and heuristic integration by introducing an extra parametric-order differential framework. By treating the order of differentiation as a parametric axis (discrete or continuous), classical integration is reframed as a local differential evaluation at the non-positive boundary level. This analytical shift alleviates some traditional routines of integration by parts, by replacing the quadrature of a product of elementary functions with a direct differential series that either truncates into a finite algebraic sum or resolves through cyclic symmetries. This parametric-order approach also bridges the gap with fractional calculus, showing that non-integer derivatives emerge as a seamless extension of the same operational dimension. By reducing global quadrature to local differentiation, this note offers an efficient, conceptual tool for undergraduate analysis.

papers.title: Point-to-ellipse series -- Part II Expansion about the center
papers.abstract: Power series expansions in the polar distance about the center are derived for the normal direction and signed distance from an ellipse to points near its center. After extracting constant terms and common factors, the series coefficients are polynomials in the axis ratio and the absolute value of the sine of the polar angle, with rational coefficients. The region of convergence is shown to be the region bounded by the ellipse evolute. The expansions complement previously derived expansions valid for points far from the center.

papers.title: Bernstein and Stieltjes properties of some functions involving logarithmic functions
papers.abstract: We show that $\frac1{g(x)}$, with $g(x)=\frac{x-1}{x\ln x}$, is a complete Bernstein function and give its L\'evy measure explicitly. For $h(x)=\frac{(x^2-1)\ln(x+1)}{x^2\ln x}$, we prove that $h$ is not a Stieltjes function, so $\frac1h$ is not a complete Bernstein function, but $\frac1h$ is a Bernstein function. The latter rests on the positivity of a function built from the convolution of the exponential integrals $E_1$ and $E_2$. We also give a related completely monotonic function that is not a Stieltjes function.

papers.title: Harborth's theorem p(5)=18 revisited
papers.abstract: Let $p(n)$ be the minimum cardinality of a finite planar point set in which each point has exactly $n$ unit-distance neighbours. Harborth proved $p(5)=18$ in work presented in 1985 and published in 1987, using a detailed case analysis. We revisit the proof using convex-hull arguments, incidence counts, and elementary properties of intersections of unit circles. These tools give an alternative treatment of configurations with $14$ and $16$ points and organize the final case distinction by a common vector-sum structure. We also treat a configuration not explicitly covered by the case analysis in the online PDF copy of Harborth's paper available to us, and give an explicit justification of the six-point classification used in the argument. No result subsequent to Harborth's proof is required.

papers.title: On Some Special Cases of the Weber-Schafheitlin Integral
papers.abstract: We consider special cases of the discontinuous Weber--Schafheitlin integral in which the orders $\mu$ and $\nu$ of the Bessel functions differ by an integer and the exponent $\lambda$ equals $0$ or $\pm1$, with $\mu-\nu+\lambda$ odd. Explicit closed-form results are obtained in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

papers.title: Derived Azumaya Algebras on Compact Derived Smooth Manifolds
papers.abstract: We extend To\"en's derived Brauer theory to the open site of Spivak's derived smooth manifolds. For a compact derived smooth manifold $X$, we define a spectralized structure sheaf $\mathbb{O}_{X}$ and prove that every Picard twist can be represented by a derived Azumaya algebra, whose Morita equivalence class is uniquely determined by the twist. In the open locally Morita trivial setting, this gives a natural bijection \begin{align*} \Phi_{X}:\mathbf{dBr}^{\mathrm{open}}(X) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{1}(|X|;\underline{\mathbb {Z}}) \times \pi_0\Gamma(|X|,\mathrm B^2GL_1(\mathbb O_X)). \end{align*} If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb C)$ on ordinary smooth manifolds, the second factor is $H^3(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z})$, which recovers the Dixmier-Douady invariant. If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb R)$, the second factor is $H^2(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z/2})$, which recovers the corresponding invariant of Donovan and Karoubi.

papers.title: Evaluations of Series Using the Beta Function
papers.abstract: This article presents proofs of seven conjectural series identities for $\pi$ proposed by Z.-W. Sun. Our proofs rely mainly on transformations involving the Beta function. We also use symbolic integration with the software \texttt{Mathematica} to reduce the amount of computational work.
